paragraphs: The 228i is a long-running variant of the F22/F23 2 Series coupe and convertible, produced from 2014 until the generation ended in 2021. Early cars (2014 to around 2016) use the N20 — a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder that was BMW's mainstay petrol engine of that era. From 2016 onwards, production switched to the B48, a newer engine architecture that's genuinely different from the N20 despite sharing the same capacity. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and the known wear pattern differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 228i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine fitted to the early 228i. Known for timing chain guide failure over time — see the callout above. We replace timing chains, guides, tensioners, and gaskets as standard on every N20 rebuild.

A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine fitted to the later 228i. Generally more reliable than the N20 — we service it to the same standard as our other 2 Series rebuilds, with timing chain, bearings, and gaskets inspected and replaced where required.

compatibility.intro: The 228i spans two distinct four-cylinder engines across its production run, and assuming an N20 part will work on a B48 car — or vice versa — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N20 or B48) via registration or VIN
Your generation (F22 or F23, though mechanically identical across coupe/convertible)
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 228i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
